title: Egg onto the table, egg onto foam
about: Two eggs fall the same height; the one onto the bare table breaks, the one onto foam does not.

source.question: Which egg breaks?
source.answer: The one that lands on the bare table.

story.says: Below one egg is the bare table; below the other, foam.
The two eggs start at the same height.
The egg on the table breaks; the egg on the foam does not.
One broken egg, one whole egg.

shots.intent: First, what each egg will land on, side by side at one scale and labelled below: the bare table in one half, foam in the other.

audit.question: Can a child see the bare table in one picture and the foam in the other?

shots.intent: Cut up to the two eggs, close, at one scale: a level line across both says they start at the same height, which makes the test fair.

audit.question: Can a child see the two eggs held at the same height?

shots.intent: Let go and ride down with both eggs, eight times slower, one camera for both halves, and come to rest at the ground as they land: one cracks on the table, one sinks into the foam.
shots.label: Slow motion: 8 times slower

audit.question: Can a child see both eggs fall and land, the one on the table breaking and the one on the foam staying whole?

shots.intent: Back to real speed, still where the camera landed, on the two results, labelled below: one broken, one whole.

audit.question: Can a child see the broken egg on the table and the whole egg on the foam?
